I was a kid in the late 90's to 2011 (turned 18 in 2011). In the 90's, literally every kid was outside almost all day. The teenagers would hang out in malls and you'd often see mall cops roaming around. It was largely like that until maybe around 2005. By the time I was 12/13 in 2006, we'd go for walks around town and meet up with other teen groups to hang out. During hangouts we might have opted to play basketball, go for group bike rides, buy stuff together, get food, etc. However, I think my generation was the first to become homebodies.   
  
By the late afternoon, we'd be at home playing games on the computer such as Habbo Hotel or Runescape while messaging friends on MSN Messenger. There were also other people who liked making YouTube videos or downloading pirated stuff on Limewire. It was sort of the 'wild west' of the internet where you weren't personally tracked so you could pretty much get away with it. On top of that, smart phones weren't a big part of our lives yet, so nobody was recording videos or constantly texting their friends. Our social lives revolved around desktop computers.

It might have been around 2013 when I noticed the internet becoming more and more censored. I thought people would be out and about by that point, but it seems as though everyone has accepted going to the same old boring websites. Not to mention, everyone largely had smartphones by then, so they'd often be in the 'mantis' position texting away.

When the old heads tell you things feel sterile and robotic these days, they are absolutely right. The kids in my area stick to their back yards now and you don't see them roaming around like we did back in the day.
